gold_answer: T1218.007: System Binary Proxy Execution: Msiexec is an attack technique that adversaries may use to launch local or network accessible MSI files, as well as execute DLLs, using the msiexec.exe binary. This technique may be used to bypass application control solutions that do not account for its potential abuse.

T1102.002: Web Service: Bidirectional Communication is an attack technique that involves using an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to and receiving output from a compromised system over the Web service channel. Compromised systems may leverage popular websites and social media to host command and control (C2) instructions.

T1055.008: Process Injection: Ptrace System Calls is an attack technique that involves injecting malicious code into processes via ptrace system calls to evade process-based defenses and possibly elevate privileges. This technique allows adversaries to execute arbitrary code in the address space of a separate live process, enabling access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly elevated privileges.

T1499.004: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation is an attack technique that involves exploiting software vulnerabilities that can cause an application or system to crash and deny availability to users. Some systems may automatically restart critical applications and services when crashes occur, but they can likely be re-exploited to cause a persistent denial of service (DoS) condition.

Adversaries may attempt to identify the primary user or set of users that commonly uses a system by retrieving account usernames or using OS Credential Dumping techniques, such as retrieving account usernames or using [OS Credential Dumping](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003).
Remote Service Session Hijacking differs from Remote Services in that it hijacks an existing session rather than creating a new session using Valid Accounts.
Obtaining and abusing credentials of a local account can be used to gain Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
